regionAvg.title: Region Average
regionAvg.description: Average composition (mean ± σ per element) over a rectangular block of pixels. Use it to measure a grain or a precipitate without picking individual pixels — pick the bounding rows and columns below.
regionAvg.computeTooltip: Sum every pixel in the rectangle, return per-element mean and standard deviation. The single-pixel quantifier above gives you one row's worth of data; this one gives you a whole region's.
regionAvg.copyTooltip: Copy region quantification to clipboard (tab-separated for Excel)

suggest.title: Phase Suggestion
suggest.description: Suggests crystal phases based on At.% at current pixel coordinates.
suggest.sourceCifTooltip: Matching against your curated CIF library (Database/crystal_database.xlsx).
suggest.sourceDefaultTooltip: No CIF database built yet — falling back to a hardcoded library of common phases. Build the database for better matches.
suggest.none: No phases suggested for this composition.
suggest.atPixelTooltip: The pixel these suggestions were computed for. Clicking another pixel on the map updates them.
suggest.staleHint: Showing an older pixel — press “Suggest Phases” for ({{row}}, {{col}}).
suggest.elementTooltip: {{el}}: measured {{measured}} at%, this phase expects {{expected}} at%. An element the phase needs but the pixel lacks is what rules it out.
suggest.thisPixelAlone: This pixel alone — the map decides by composition group:

noMatch.notEnriched: {{phase}} fits this pixel ({{score}}) but was rejected: {{element}} is {{measured}} at% here, against a map background of {{background}} at%. A phase needing {{element}} is only assigned above {{required}} at%, so a phase that makes up most of the map can never clear that bar — and the phase map applies the same rule, so it leaves those pixels unassigned too. Name the region by hand in the phase map, or crop to an area where the phase is a minority, if there is one.
noMatch.belowMinScore: The closest phase in the library, {{phase}}, only scores {{score}} against this chemistry (minimum {{min}}).
noMatch.noCandidate: No phase in the library is built only from the elements this pixel shows ({{elements}}).
noMatch.emptyLibrary: No CIF phases available — put CIF files in Database/CIF_Library or build the CIF database.
noMatch.noChemistry: This pixel carries no EDS chemistry to match.

swipe.handleTooltip: Drag to slide the A/B split

threshold.convertToMaskTooltip: Hide everything outside this threshold. Pixels outside the range vanish from the layers underneath too, so only what you kept stays visible.

phaseMap.title: Phase Map Builder
phaseMap.toleranceInert: Tolerance has no effect. It is still accepted and stored, but the classifier never reads it — it was superseded and left in place for compatibility. It is not part of a preset.
phaseMap.minScoreTooltip: Pixels below this match score are left unclassified
phaseMap.autoClassifyTooltip: Match every pixel against the curated CIF library

confirmReclassify.title: Rebuild the regions?
confirmReclassify.bodyOne: Classifying again builds the regions from scratch, so the {{count}} name you gave by hand is discarded.
confirmReclassify.bodyOther: Classifying again builds the regions from scratch, so the {{count}} names you gave by hand are discarded.
confirmReclassify.kept: Pixels you painted by hand are kept. Painting locks a pixel; naming a region does not — that is the whole difference.

phaseMap.noMapHintPost: to assign each pixel its closest CIF phase.
phaseMap.canvasPolygonTooltip: Click to add a vertex; close with the Close polygon button
phaseMap.canvasRectTooltip: Click to inspect, drag to select a region
phaseMap.readout: Pixel ({{row}}, {{col}}) — drag a rectangle to paint a region, click a legend phase to assign it.
phaseMap.assignRegionTooltipNoPhase: Pick a phase from the legend first
phaseMap.polygonHint: Click on the map to add vertices ({{count}} placed{{suffix}}).
phaseMap.closeAssignTooltipNoPhase: Pick a phase from the legend first
phaseMap.closeAssignTooltipNeedMore: Need at least 3 vertices to form a polygon
phaseMap.closeAssignTooltip: Close & assign polygon ({{count}} vertices) to phase #{{phase}}
phaseMap.sendToIndexingTooltip: Send phase classification to the Indexing module so each phase is tested only on its assigned pixels
phaseMap.modeTooltip: Clusters: group pixels of similar composition and match each group's mean — more reliable, because a single pixel's composition carries several at% of measurement error. Per pixel: match every pixel on its own.
phaseMap.nClustersTooltip: Number of composition groups. Leave on auto and it is chosen by the spatial coherence of the resulting map.
phaseMap.phaseSelectionTooltip: Untick a phase to keep it out of the classification. Useful when two library entries are chemically indistinguishable.
phaseMap.ambiguousTooltip: Another phase from a different group scored within 0.01 — chemistry cannot separate them here.
phaseMap.undoTooltip: Take back the last change ({{what}}). One level.
phaseMap.replaceTooltip: Repoint every pixel of one phase at another. For a classifier error that covers a large part of the map, where selecting by hand is not practical.
phaseMap.replaceGo: Replace every pixel of that phase with the one selected in the legend
phaseMap.replaceNeedTarget: Pick the target phase in the legend first
phaseMap.replaceHint: Target is whichever phase is selected in the legend.
phaseMap.colorTooltip: Click to recolour {{name}}, right-click to reset. The colour is shared with the EBSD phase map.
phaseMap.colorHint: Click a swatch to recolour · right-click resets
phaseMap.scaleUnitTooltip: Whether the smoothing box is set in pixels or in micrometres. A pixel width is a different physical box on every scan: 5 px is a 2.5 µm box at a 0.5 µm step and a 3.75 µm box at a 0.75 µm step — the same setting, a 50 % different analysis. Set in µm, the same recipe averages over the same area on any scan, and the pixel count is worked out from this file’s step size.
phaseMap.scaleResolvedXY: Last run: {{px}} px = {{x}} × {{y}} µm box (the step differs along x and y)
phaseMap.scaleResolvedPxOnly: Last run: {{px}} px — this scan carries no step size, so the box cannot be given as a length.
phaseMap.scaleNoStep: A {{um}} µm box was requested, but this scan carries no step size — {{px}} px was used instead. The width is not the physical one you asked for.
phaseMap.scaleNotApplicable: Per-pixel classification averages nothing, so no smoothing width was used.
phaseMap.minScoreNote: Every pixel is scored from 0 to 1 for how well its chemistry fits a phase. Raise this and the map keeps only the confident calls and shows more grey.
phaseMap.toleranceRemoved: The old Tolerance slider is gone: no part of the classifier ever read it. Min score is the control that decides what stays unclassified.

warnings.title: Before you quote this map
warnings.scoring_ignores_c_and_o: {{elements}} carry {{mean}} at% of the composition in this scan, and phase scoring drops them before it compares anything. Every phase here was matched on its metal content alone: an oxide or a carbide scores exactly like the metal it contains — Al₂O₃ cannot be told from Al — so a named metal may be sitting where the oxide is. Confirm any phase whose identity rests on C or O by another method before quoting this map.
warnings.indistinguishable_after_excluding_c_and_: {{n}} candidate pair(s) become indistinguishable once carbon and oxygen are dropped for scoring: {{pairs}}. Their scores can never differ on any pixel, so which of them the map names is decided by the tie-break and not by the measured chemistry. Where one of these is reported, treat the other as equally likely.
warnings.phase_has_no_scoreable_chemistry: {{n}} candidate phase(s) are made only of elements the scorer discards: {{phases}}. Nothing is left to compare, so they score neutral against every pixel — where one of them wins, it won by tie-break rather than by chemistry.

handEdits.untracked: Hand edits were not recorded for this map — it was restored from a sidecar written before edits were tracked. That is not the same as none.
handEdits.none: No hand edits — this map is exactly as it was classified.
handEdits.regionGridEdited: Region boundaries were edited after classification, so region-derived particle ids have been renumbered — ids on a figure made before those edits no longer point at the same particles.

hoverTips.pixelCol: Column index of the pixel to quantify

hoverTips.regionRowStart: First row of the averaging rectangle
hoverTips.regionRowEnd: Last row of the averaging rectangle (inclusive)
hoverTips.regionColStart: First column of the averaging rectangle
hoverTips.regionColEnd: Last column of the averaging rectangle (inclusive)
hoverTips.suggestRun: Suggest crystal phases from the At.% at the selected pixel
hoverTips.toleranceSlider: Drag to set the per-element At.% deviation that scores 0
hoverTips.minScoreSlider: Drag to set the minimum match score for a pixel to be classified
hoverTips.paintModeRectangle: Paint regions by dragging an axis-aligned rectangle
hoverTips.paintModePolygon: Paint regions by clicking polygon vertices
hoverTips.colorInput: Pick a new display color for this element
hoverTips.resetColors: Reset all element colors to their defaults

wand.modeTooltip: Click a feature to select everything chemically like it, then set how far the selection reaches.
wand.hint: Click a feature on the map to select it.
wand.sliderTooltip: How far the selection reaches. The axis is the pixel count, because thresholding the chemistry directly has dead bands. A sudden jump means the selection has escaped into the matrix.
wand.enrichmentTooltip: How many times the map's own background level each element reaches in this selection. Below about 1.3x the classifier itself cannot tell feature from background.
wand.assignTooltip: Assign the selected phase to these pixels
wand.assignTooltipNoPhase: Pick a phase from the legend first
wand.scopeConnectedTooltip: Grow outward from the pixel you clicked, stopping at the feature's edge.
wand.scopeAllTooltip: Select every pixel on the map with a similar composition, not just this one feature. A phase is rarely a single blob.

regions.viewRegionsTooltip: What the map is made of: pixels grouped by element ratio alone, before anything is named.
regions.viewPhasesTooltip: The same map seen through the names you gave the regions.
regions.none: This map has no regions. Re-run the classification in “Clusters” mode.
regions.unnamed: not named yet — pick a phase below
regions.scaleTooltip: How far the composition is averaged before grouping. Larger gives tidier regions but absorbs features thinner than the box. Off is the honest raw signal and usually unusable: on a real scan it left thousands of separate pieces with a median size of one pixel.
regions.countTooltip: How many groups to cut the map into. Leave empty to let the data decide: the count rises while the group compositions stay distinguishable, and stops when they start duplicating each other.
regions.reclassifyHint: Both take effect on the next classification.
regions.nameTooltip: Put {{name}} on every pixel of this region
regions.clearNameTooltip: Take the name off this region; its pixels become unclassified
regions.mergeTooltip: Fold another region into this one. The tool this data needs most: EDS taken during an EBSD session has an interaction volume far larger than the features, so a small particle reads as a dilution gradient rather than a plateau and gets cut into concentric rings. How much rim belongs to the particle is your call.
regions.splitTooltip: Re-group this region's own pixels, leaving the rest of the map untouched. Raising the region count instead would re-cut every other region too.
regions.growTooltip: Push this region's edge out or pull it in by one pixel. Blind to the chemistry — use Snap for that.
regions.snapTooltip: Let every boundary relax onto the nearest strong chemistry edge. The slider sets how wide a band around each boundary is put up for re-decision; the regions' interiors always keep their identity, so nothing can vanish or swap.
regions.handToolsHint: Naming a whole region is one click. The hand tools are below for anything the grouping cannot express.
regions.handToolsTooltip: Rectangle, polygon, wand and map-wide replacement. These belong to the phase view and are folded away while you are grouping.
regions.howStep1: 1 — The map is cut into REGIONS by element ratio alone. A region is just "these pixels have the same chemistry"; it has no name yet, and its colour means nothing beyond telling it apart from its neighbours.
regions.howStep2: 2 — You give each region a phase. Several regions may get the SAME phase — that is normal and expected, which is why one phase name appears on several rows in the list.
regions.howStep3: 3 — Switch to “Phases” to see the result: one colour per phase, so two neighbouring regions you gave the same phase become one uninterrupted area. Many regions, few phases.
regions.pixelModeNoRegions: Per-pixel mode has no regions, so any names you gave them are gone. Switch back to Clusters and re-classify to get them back.
regions.countRestTooltip: How many groups to cut the UNDECLARED part of the map into. The regions you defined by composition are already fixed and are not re-cut.
regions.countRestNote: {{count}} region(s) are defined by composition and stay as they are.

defs.explain: Group the map yourself instead of letting the fit decide. Useful when what separates two regions is one specific element rather than the overall composition — pure Si and AlFeMnSi differ by a few at% of iron on top of the same aluminium background, and unweighted distance is almost entirely that aluminium.
defs.weightsExplain: Keeps the grouping automatic but tells it what to care about. A weight multiplies one element's contribution to the distance; no composition you see anywhere changes. Reach for it when the elements that separate your regions are small but present everywhere. It is not always enough — if weighting does not separate them, define the region instead.
defs.addTooltip: An empty definition, to fill in below
defs.seedTooltip: Start from the region you picked on the map: its own composition, widened to ±2 spreads, over the elements enriched there
defs.seedDisabledTooltip: Pick a region on the map first
defs.none: No definitions yet. The grouping runs automatically, and everything below is for the regions it keeps getting wrong.
defs.elementTooltip: This element must lie inside this window, in renormalised at%. Leave a side empty for no bound.
defs.moveUpTooltip: Move up. Order is priority: the first definition that matches a pixel keeps it.
defs.moveDownTooltip: Move down. Order is priority: the first definition that matches a pixel keeps it.
defs.emptyWarning: No composition window yet — this claims nothing.
defs.remainderTooltip: On: the definitions claim their pixels and the rest of the map is clustered as usual. Off: the map is exactly what you declared, plus one region holding everything else.
defs.previewTooltip: Count what each window would claim on this map, without changing anything
defs.previewOverlap: ({{px}} px went to an earlier definition)
defs.previewRowTooltip: What this window claimed on the real map. An overlap is normal — the first definition that matches keeps the pixel.
defs.applyTooltip: Re-run the classification with these definitions and weights. The regions are rebuilt, so if you named any of them by hand you are asked to confirm first. Pixels you painted are kept.
defs.ratioTooltip: The ratio of one element to another must lie in this range. Survives a change in matrix level that an absolute at% threshold does not. Pixels where either element is at noise level are treated as undecidable and excluded.
defs.enrichmentTooltip: This element must be at least this many times its level in the surrounding map. Usually the most robust clause, and the one that carries over to another dataset: the background is re-measured per map, an absolute at% is not.
defs.clauseHint: Content is an absolute window in at%. A ratio is one element per another. Enrichment is relative to this map's own background, and is usually the sturdiest of the three: on a real particle a 2× enrichment window kept 96% of it while an absolute at% threshold set to match kept 46%.
defs.previewMeanTooltip: The average composition of the pixels this window caught. The count alone cannot tell you whether you caught the right ones - 202 px of matrix and 202 px of particle look identical until you see what is in them.
defs.weightZero: A weight of 0 leaves the element out of the grouping entirely.

reason.taken: every matching pixel was already claimed by a definition above

defs.fromPixelTooltip: Point at a pixel that is clearly the thing you want — the middle of a particle — and a window is written from what it actually contains. This is where the numbers come from: a threshold for a silicon particle has to be read off a silicon pixel, not off a region that failed to separate it.
defs.seedPixelNothing: Nothing is concentrated at ({{row}}, {{col}}) — that pixel reads like the surrounding matrix. Pick one inside the feature you want.
defs.firstMove: Start here: press “From a pixel…”, then click the middle of the particle the grouping is lumping together. Press “Try it” and the pixels that window claims light up on the map — widen or narrow the number until they match what you see.

inspector.title: Region inspector
inspector.empty: Click a region on the map, or a row in the list, to inspect it.
inspector.headline: {{px}} px · {{pct}}% of the map
inspector.piecesTooltip: How many separate parts this region is in, largest first. Three concentric rings of one particle show up here as three pieces of similar size — that is the sign to merge.
inspector.spreadTooltip: Standard deviation inside the region. A region that is not homogeneous is either two things or a gradient.
inspector.enrichmentTooltip: How many times the map's own background level this element reaches here, measured on the composition shown above. A window is judged on the smoothed composition instead, so on a feature smaller than the smoothing box the two differ - use “Define this region by composition” rather than copying these numbers by hand. Below about 1.3× the classifier cannot tell feature from background.
inspector.neighbourTooltip: Largest single-element difference: {{gap}} at%, over {{edge}} px of shared edge. Click to inspect it. A small gap on a long shared edge usually means one region cut in two.
inspector.candidateTooltip: {{name}} is {{gap}} at% off on average. Click to put it on the whole region.
inspector.compositionHint: Average of every pixel in this region. ± is how much the pixels differ from that average — a large ± means the region is not one thing.
inspector.neighboursHint: Regions this one borders on. The number is the biggest difference in any single element. A small number on a long border usually means one region got cut in two — merge it.
inspector.candidatesHint: Library phases sorted by how close their formula is to the measured composition. Click one to put it on the whole region.
inspector.scaleLegend: vs background: 1.0× means this element is no more common here than anywhere else on the map. Above 1.3× it is genuinely concentrated here; below 0.77× it is depleted.
inspector.defineTooltip: Turn this region into a composition window you can adjust: its own values, widened to ±2 spreads. Opens in 'Define regions'.

rollup.headline: {{regions}} regions → {{phases}} phases
rollup.explain: The list above names a phase once per region, so a phase covering four regions is written four times. Here it is counted once.
rollup.unnamedTooltip: Regions with no phase yet. They are drawn as unclassified in the phase view.
rollup.showPhasesTooltip: One colour per phase. Neighbouring regions you gave the same phase become one uninterrupted area there.

tabs.elementsTooltip: The composite overlay, the layer stack and every element map side by side.
tabs.phaseMapTooltip: Group the map by chemistry into regions, then decide which phase each one is.
tabs.noMapYet: No phase map yet. Use Auto-Classify on the right to build one from the chemistry.

background.label: Under the map
background.tooltip: Lay one element map or electron image under the phase map, so a region can be placed against the chemistry or the topography it came from.
background.opacityTooltip: How solid the phase map is. The MAP fades, not the image beneath it - the map is the thing you are placing.
background.fovWarning: The image below covers a {{pct}}% different field of view, so it may not line up.

rules.explain: A rule decides which phases may COMPETE for a region — not how well they score. A phase whose rule fails simply cannot win there; the region goes to the next candidate, or stays unclassified and says which rule blocked it. Rules only take effect on the next classification.
rules.withRulesHint: Everything else is decided automatically, as before.
rules.noneYet: No rules yet. Select a region on the map, then seed one from it.
rules.seedTooltip: Start a rule for {{name}} from what this region actually measures — mean ± 2× the spread, on the elements that are genuinely concentrated here. Then correct the numbers.
rules.seedNeedRegion: Select a region on the map first
rules.pickOne: Pick a phase on the left to edit its rules.
rules.allMustHold: Every line must hold. Ranges are at% of the measured elements, with C and O left out — the same composition the inspector shows.
rules.enrichmentHint: Enrichment is measured against this map's own background, so it needs no k-factor and travels between datasets. On a real particle “Si ≥ 2× background” kept 96 % of it where “Si ≥ 40 at%” kept 46 %.
rules.applyTooltip: Re-run the classification with these rules. The regions are rebuilt, so if you named any of them by hand you are asked to confirm first. Pixels you painted are kept.
rules.matrixHint: the element the sample is made of, e.g. Al
rules.matrixTooltip: Which element is the solvent. It is inferred when left on automatic; declare it when the inference would be wrong — the scoring is built around this choice, so getting it wrong inverts the whole measure. It is exempt from the penalty for unexplained elements and from the enrichment bar, but it stays in the composition: dropping it and renormalising lifted a pure aluminium matrix from Si 1.2 to 46.3 at% on a real scan, which would make the matrix look like a phase.

export.alwaysWritten: provenance.json is always written. It is the record of what you did, and it is what makes the numbers defensible.
export.areaMissing: This scan carries no step size, so area_um2, ecd_um and every other length column is left out completely. A wrong scale is worse than no scale. Pixel counts are unaffected, and the reason is recorded in provenance.json.
export.areaMissingTitle: No step size — no µm columns
export.areaOk: Step size {{x}} × {{y}} µm — areas are written in µm².

art.phases: phases.csv — one row per phase, plus an unclassified row
art.regions: regions.csv — one row per region (assigned phase = column phase_final)
art.particles: particles.csv — one row per connected particle (assigned phase = column phase_name)
art.definitions: definitions.csv — every region definition and what it claimed. Phase rules are not in this file; they are written to provenance.json under classification.rules.
art.xlsx: summary.xlsx — all of the above, one sheet each
art.labels: labels.npz — region and phase id rasters (large)
art.pixels: pixels.csv — one row per pixel (very large)

artTip.phases: Unclassified is a row of its own, not a leftover: the area that received no phase is a result.
artTip.regions: A region is a chemistry group spanning the whole map; several regions can carry the same phase name. Its assigned phase is the column phase_final — the same thing is called phase_name in particles.csv, phases.csv and pixels.csv.
artTip.particles: A particle is one connected component. Sizes, shapes and positions, plus touches_edge — a particle at the image edge is truncated and its size is only a lower bound. Its assigned phase is the column phase_name — the same thing is called phase_final in regions.csv.
artTip.definitions: What each window and rule claimed, so a reader can follow the run without the app.
artTip.xlsx: For reading. The CSVs are the machine-readable copy.
artTip.labels: The id rasters, for redoing the arithmetic in your own script.
artTip.pixels: One row per pixel. Grows with the scan — a large map produces a file no spreadsheet will open.

export.buttonTooltip: Write the phases, regions, particles and the full record of how they were produced into a folder.
export.checkedAgainst: Checked against {{file}} on {{when}}. This travels into provenance.json with the export.
export.clash: A comma cannot be both the decimal separator and the column separator — every value would split across two columns. Choose a semicolon or a tab.
export.conn4Tooltip: Only edge neighbours count as the same particle. Diagonal chains are split.
export.conn8Tooltip: Corner neighbours count too. The usual choice, and the default.
export.connectivityTooltip: Which neighbours make two pixels the same particle. It changes the particle count, so the figures above are recounted when you change it.
export.copyFailed: Could not reach the clipboard — select the text and copy it by hand.
export.copyTooltip: Copy the summary line to the clipboard.
export.destPlaceholder: Folder to write the export into
export.minPxNote: Nothing is deleted. Rows below the limit are marked below_size_limit and stay in the file, so the count you export is the count that was measured.
export.needMap: Classify the map first — there is nothing to count yet.
export.overrideNote: The preset “{{name}}” was applied over a refusal. The refusal is written into provenance.json.
export.presetNote: The preset “{{name}}” is recorded in provenance.json.

sum.particlesFlagged: {{particles}} particles ({{below}} below the {{limit}} px limit, {{edge}} touching the edge).
sum.semiQuant: Semi-quantitative: no full ZAF correction, no standard calibration.

export.summaryHint: Everything in it comes from provenance.json. A clause this run could not supply is left out rather than guessed.
export.title: Export EDS phase data

warn.no_acquisition_header: The EDS acquisition header could not be read, so the beam voltage, working distance, detector and spectrometer settings are absent from this export. Every measured number is unaffected.
warn.no_step_size: This file carries no step size for the EDS or EBSD grid, so every column in micrometres has been omitted. A guessed scale would look like an answer.
warn.no_valid_eds: No pixel in this raster carries a usable EDS measurement; frac_of_valid_eds is empty throughout.
warn.nothing_classified: No pixel received a phase; frac_of_classified is empty throughout.
warn.particle_scale_failed: The step size was rejected while scaling particles; the micrometre columns are incomplete.
warn.particles_from_phases: This map has no regions (it was classified per pixel), so particles are connected components of the PHASE grid. Two regions carrying the same phase would be one particle here.
warn.region_ids_renumbered: The region grid was edited after classification (a merge, split, grow or edge snap). Region ids and particle ids are ordered by (region_id, -n_px, centroid), so those edits RENUMBER them: an id written on an earlier figure may now mean a different region.

presets.title: Preset
presets.applyTooltip: Check this preset against the loaded scan, and apply it only if it fits.
presets.saveAsTooltip: Write the current settings to a preset file. Nothing bound to this one scan is included.
presets.importTooltip: Read a preset file somebody sent you.
presets.exportFileTooltip: Write the selected preset out as a JSON file.
presets.deleteConfirm: Delete the preset “{{name}}”? The file is removed.
presets.blockedTitle: This preset does not fit this scan
presets.blockedHint: Nothing has been applied. Fix the mismatch, or apply it anyway — the refusal is then written into the export, so the result stays defensible.
presets.applyAnywayTooltip: Apply despite the refusal. The refusal travels into provenance.json with the export.
presets.appliedOverride: Applied “{{name}}” over a refusal — this is recorded in the export.
presets.saveAuthorPlaceholder: Who wrote it — a preset with no author is a rumour
presets.saveNotesPlaceholder: What it is for, and on what material
presets.saveHint: Saved: mode, the smoothing width (as a length when you set one in µm, so it means the same box on a scan with a different step size), region count, min score, element weights, region definitions, rules and the phases taking part. Not saved: file paths, the crop, hand-painted pixels or anything else bound to this one scan.
presets.toleranceInert: Tolerance is not part of a preset — it has no effect on the result.
presets.saveMaterialPlaceholder: e.g. AA6061, cast Al-Si, low-alloy steel
presets.saveMaterialTooltip: What material this recipe is for. It is what makes a preset findable once there are a hundred of them.
presets.saveTagsPlaceholder: Comma separated, e.g. rolled, qa, customer 4711
presets.saveTagsTooltip: Free labels to find this preset by later - your group, a project, an instrument. Separate them with commas. Existing tags are offered as you type, so the same tag does not end up spelt two ways.
presets.saveMatrixTooltip: The element this recipe assumes the matrix is. It is the strongest of the compatibility refusals: an aluminium recipe applied to a steel is then refused outright rather than merely warned about. Left unset, the element pinned in the rules is used if there is one.
presets.authoredAgainst: Recorded with this preset: authored against {{elements}}. No step size is known yet — run a classification first if you want it recorded.
presets.authoredAgainstStep: Recorded with this preset: authored against {{elements}} at a {{step}} µm step. A scan with a different element list or step size is then warned about.
presets.authoredAgainstNothing: No element list could be read from this scan, so nothing is recorded about what this preset was authored against — the two compatibility warnings that need it cannot fire.
